pumac-2014-combinatorics-a-02.prompt: Assume you have a magical pizza in the shape of an infinite plane. You have a magical pizza cutter that can cut in the shape of an infinite line, but it can only be used $14$ times. To share with as many of your friends as possible, you cut the pizza in a way that maximizes the number of finite pieces (the infinite pieces have infinite mass, so you can't lift them up). How many finite pieces of pizza do you have?

pumac-2014-combinatorics-a-03.prompt: You have three colours $\{$red, blue, green$\}$ with which you can colour the faces of a regular octahedron (an $8$-sided polyhedron with triangular faces, made of two square-based pyramids stuck together at their bases), but you must do so in a way that avoids colouring adjacent faces (faces sharing an edge) with the same colour. How many different colouring schemes are possible? (Two colouring schemes are considered equivalent if one can be rotated to fit the other.)

pumac-2014-combinatorics-a-05.prompt: What is the size of the largest subset $S'$ of $S=\{2^x3^y5^z:0\le x,y,z\le4\}$ such that there are no distinct elements $p,q\in S'$ with $p\mid q$?

pumac-2014-combinatorics-a-06.prompt: Let $f(n)$ be the number of points of intersection of diagonals of an $n$-dimensional hypercube that are not vertices of the cube. For example, $f(3)=7$ because the intersection points of a cube's diagonals are at the centres of each face and the centre of the cube. Find $f(5)$.

pumac-2014-combinatorics-a-07.prompt: Ding and Jianing are playing a game. In this game, they use pieces of paper with $2014$ positions, in which some permutation of the numbers $1,2,\dots,2014$ is to be written (each number exactly once). Ding fills in a piece of paper first. How many pieces of paper must Jianing fill in to ensure that at least one of her pieces of paper will have a permutation that has the same number as Ding's in at least one position?
